pivot.measured: not measured on the real duck: the real duck's pivot is not measured here
pivot.why: The real duck pivots backward by upstream (RFC-0008 §4) and keeps 0 until its pivot is measured.

pace.measured: RFC-0012 section 3: caution is the slowest reliable walk (locomotion.slowest_mps: the duck does not walk below 0.2 m/s and creep is the same speed), the look distance 0.7 m is the drops' (cliff.LOOK_M), the unseen floor's reach 0.4 m is the far edge of the look-before-you-step strip (RFC-0012 section 2.1). Not tuned: taken as those. Effect measured 2026-11-19 on challenges 6, 7, 10 and 11, seeds 1-3 x 2 repeats, against the base c79fe6b (one pace, 0.3 m/s): passed 1/6, 0/6, 6/6, 6/6 became 2/6, 0/6, 6/6, 6/6; refusals 11 became 10; contacts and falls 0 and 0; the closest approach to an obstacle (truth) 0.152, 0.146, 0.488, 0.178 m became 0.151, 0.155, 0.481, 0.185 m; the mean time of a run 16.7, 12.4, 42.3, 42.8 s became 24.5, 13.0, 49.5, 49.4 s. 79 % of the straight walking was at caution; unseen floor started 12 of 15 caution spells in challenge 10 and 6 of 8 in 11 (the map grows at stops, so floor just ahead is often unseen): no gain in refusals or closeness, about 15 % more time on 10 and 11. caution_mps = cruise_mps turns the pace off.
pace.why: pace is chosen from the map ahead so the duck slows before it arrives: a known drop beside the way (within the error budget's drop_inflate_m + corridor_m of the path), a narrow passage (an obstacle within slow_clearance_m of the path) or floor the map has not seen, within look_m of the path.

closure.measured: 2026-11-20, robots/duck/sim/probes/closure_replay.py over the 1614 recorded runs (the data folder and the phase 4 safety runs): mapd's loop counter stepped in 2, and both closures, taken unchecked, made the belief worse (explore-p4s-fix-r2 at 318.8 s: the belief moved 2.279 m and 0.70 rad, error 0.11 -> 2.22 m; explore-p4s-base-r2 at 250.0 s: moved 0.427 m, error 0.17 -> 0.37 m). After each, the belief's error vector changed by at most 0.11 m in 15 s: mapd's later fixes stayed on the closure's frame, so fixes agreeing with the closure (hold_n of them within hold_agree_m) do not tell a wrong closure from a right one. A landmark seen under the closure's frame does: in base-r2 the coat rack sat 0.36-0.52 m off its anchor under it (7 verdicts, all 'disagrees', 2 more 'refused'), and in fix-r2 no anchored landmark was within match_m of where the closure put the duck. The relocaliser's own median against the truth, 12 corrections in 6 runs: p50 0.127 m, p90 0.194 m, max 0.322 m. No right closure was recorded, so the tolerance is not measured against one.
closure.why: A loop closure mapd believed was taken at once (K26), and both seen were wrong. It is held like any large fix, and taken only when min_n sightings within spread_m of each other, placed as the closure's frame would place the duck, put the anchored landmarks within this of their anchors: the relocaliser's p90 error, since a closer agreement cannot be told from its noise, and about the belief's own error before the two closures (0.11 and 0.17 m). With no landmark in sight it stays held.

anomalies.measured: 2026-11-19, the 66 recordings of the apartment scene (simulator). Head: 160107 walking samples (a forward command) of 63 runs; the pose is each joint's median over the runs' medians; a sample within 0.10 rad of it in 81 %, over 0.30 rad from it in 12 %; episodes of 1 s or more over 0.30 rad: 209 in 20 runs, and 1 each in b9 r2, b10b r1 and b11 r1, 2 in b10b r2 (over 0.20 rad: 8 and 9 in b10b r1 and r2). Streams: the longest gap between state samples 1.40 s and between depth frames 1.41 s, except apartment-1117c (25 s). Refusals for no room to turn (sim/probes/room_rule.py, the 231 of 240 with depth frames; 'the map wrong' is its room more than 5 cm tighter than the truth at the truth pose; base rate 35 of 231, 15 %): the rule before, a nearest return ahead of 280 mm or more, flagged 114 and the map was wrong in 16 (14 %, no better than the base rate); the rule now (the map's nearest obstacle within room_disagrees_near_m, the returns of the last room_disagrees_window_s within room_disagrees_look_deg of its bearing and room_disagrees_see_m: 'disagrees' = floor at or beyond it, less room_disagrees_floor_slack_m, and no obstacle return at or nearer than it plus room_disagrees_agree_m) flags 22 and the map was wrong in 8 (36 %, 2.4 times the base rate; recall 8 of 35); 101 agree (12 wrong), 107 unseen (15 wrong, no verdict), 1 unclear; 14 of the 22 are refusals where the map's room was within 5 cm of the truth's (why the sensor read floor there is not examined). No-path refusals with a free start, a goal that is not lethal and nothing within 0.30 m of the pose by the cost map: 8 of 181, in 2 runs (b10b r1, b12 r2)
anomalies.why: the thresholds of the robot-tagged anomalies that are the duck's (RFC-0019 step 1, PHASE3-PREP B1): the head's walking pose and how far from it counts as off (a glance that left the head pitched tilted the odometry), how long the state and depth streams may be silent before they are stale (3 s is more than twice the longest gap of a running run), what makes a refusal for no room to turn disagree with the map (the map's nearest obstacle within 0.6 m of the pose; the depth returns of the last 4 s within 20 deg of its bearing and 1.5 m, from the sensor's own frames: an obstacle return at or nearer than the map's distance plus 8 cm agrees, floor at or beyond it, 2 cm slack, and none near it disagrees; the numbers are the ones K36's probe was run with, not tuned), and the distance round the pose inside which something in the map explains a refusal; how many refused legs at one pose (within refusal_burst_moved_m) make a burst (the 66 recordings grouped refused legs by pose 1: 81, 2: 18, 3: 16, 4: 3, 5: 3, 6 or more: 35; 3 is the first count past one or two bad targets, three legs before the explorer calls it trapped); and when an anomaly at one place is said again (the duck moved same_place_moved_m, or same_place_gap_s passed: b11 r5 refused six targets in 1 s at one pose). Accepted by the operator 2026-11-19. Measured in the simulator only; the real duck has its own measurement to make (its walking head pose is robotd's default, neck 13 deg and head 20 deg, SIDE-DROPS.md)

odometry.measured: 2026-11-14, robots/duck/sim/probes/odom_vs_truth.py (straight walks, 3 x 8 s per speed, truth = body server trunk) and robots/duck/sim/odom_scale.py over ~41 m of navigation logs (0.909). Re-measured 2026-11-19 on the same probe, 4 x 8 s per speed: truth/odometry 0.856 at 0.2, 0.893 at 0.25, 0.913 at 0.3, 0.940 at 0.4, each within the runs' own spread (0.84-0.88 at 0.2), so the table stands. In navigation (robots/duck/sim/odom_by_speed.py, 440 runs, belief over truth with `scale` alone): 0.995 at 0.3 straight (826.8 m), 0.986 at 0.3 turning (111.8 m), 0.986 at 0.2 on arcs (7.9 m); no straight 0.2 walk is in those runs.
odometry.why: robotd's odometry reads ~10 % long in the simulator and mapd builds its map from it; the navigator scales odometry, mapd's poses and mapd's grid by this factor (operator, 2026-11-14: options 2 and 3). The simulator's odometry reads longer the slower the duck walks (K8), so the navigator's own dead reckoning between fixes scales each step by the table's value at the speed commanded while a straight walk (a turn under straight_rad_s, the navigator's slow_yaw_rad_s) was walked; `scale` stays the map's and mapd's pose's metres, and corrects pivots and arcs (arcs at 0.2 m/s measured right with it, 0.986). A real duck gets its own measurement (phase 5). Remove when robotd or mapd corrects it upstream.

pivot.measured: 2026-11-16. A turn on the spot creeps the way the duck faces: 0.27 m per full turn, p95 0.54 m, from the truth over the challenge course (robots/duck/sim/probes/turn_drift.py). robots/duck/sim/probes/pivot_counter.py, ch5-s3, a half turn to the right at 0.8 rad/s, one sample each: moved 0.111 m with vx 0, 0.058 m with -0.035, 0.026 m with -0.06.
pivot.why: a U-turn in a 60 cm corridor (challenge 5) ended 8-11 cm toward the side it turned to and was refused for no room to turn: 6/10 with vx 0. With -0.06 sent during a pivot: 10/10, twice; challenges 1, 3, 8, 9 10/10, challenge 2 9/10 (seed 5 stalled after a detour that began before any pivot; 3/3 on a rerun). A side-choice before a large turn (from the map, then from a head glance) was tried first: 6/10 and 3/10, dropped. The real duck pivots backward by upstream (RFC-0008 §4) and keeps 0 until its pivot is measured.

mount.measured: 2026-11-16. Range: the simulator's tof.py casts unit rays (mj_ray) and reports the hit distance along each, so readings are radial. Pitch: robots/duck/sim/probes/floor_fit.py over the challenge course's 40 flat-floor runs, the offset (0 to 4 deg in 0.5 deg steps with radial readings, and the real duck's 3 deg axial) that puts the recorded floor returns at floor height; 2.5 deg radial places them at +5.5 to -3.7 mm from 0.3 to 0.9 m (mean |error| 2.8 mm, the smallest), 0 deg radial 16 to 32 mm high (23.2), 3 deg axial 6 to 18 mm low (14.6). The servo joints alone (tof_truth.py, which leaves the model's passive backlash hinges at 0) put the optical axis 3.0 deg less steep than 3 deg believed: the extra ~2.5 deg is not in the servo angles, most likely the head sagging on its backlash hinges (not measured directly).
mount.why: with the real duck's values (3 deg, axial) the cliff check placed the floor up to 2 cm too low and, with the head near level (the walk's first second, the neck pitched up ~13 deg), stopped for drops that were not there: 131 frames and 8 cliff stops in the challenge course's 40 runs on flat floor (robots/duck/sim/probes/cliff_replay.py). 0 deg also removed them but by placing the floor too high, which made the check blind to the first 2-3 cm of any drop. The real duck keeps mapd's 3 deg and axial ranges (cliff.py's defaults); whether the real sensor's ranges are axial is not checked here.

camera.why: The simulated camera's fidelity (RFC-0016, duck_lab/nav/sim_camera.py): guesses, not measured, until a real camera and detector are. Field of view and range of recognition, the probability of recognising an object in view (falling to half at range), range noise in proportion, bearing noise in degrees, how often it looks.
